title: Open a Markdown folder and see it as a map
subtitle: Open a folder of Markdown files on this Mac and Atlas draws its concepts as a map. The files stay on this Mac and Atlas does not upload them; a coding agent you connect later may send prompts and context to its own provider.
openBody: Pick an existing Markdown folder to use as your ontology folder.
justStartBody: Creates it under Ontology Atlas in your home folder, with no picker. Your coding agent can read and write it too.
justStartToast: Created at {path}: your coding agent can see this folder too.
createBody: Pick an empty folder and Atlas adds 5 starter Markdown files and agent settings.
starterFailed: The folder opened, but its starter files could not be written. Add them from Settings › Ontology folder.
errorFallback: Could not open the folder. Try again.
errorRootRejected: This folder can't be used as a map. Pick a folder that holds your documents, not a system folder or your whole home folder.
trustLine: Your Markdown files are the source of truth · no Atlas server
errorPathMissing: That folder is gone. It looks like it was moved or deleted. Pick another one.
errorGrantNeeded: After this update, choose your ontology folder once to confirm access. Your documents are still there.
errorPermissionDenied: macOS is protecting the folder “{folder}”. Allow Ontology Atlas in System Settings under Privacy & Security, then Files and Folders, and open it again.
shapeTitle: Pick what to start with. The folder gets the same tree either way, and you can add the other part later from Settings.
shapeWikiBody: Your files go in sources/, and an agent writes one wiki page per document. No map, no code needed.
shapeMapBody: Starter concepts and agent skills for describing what the code builds and why. No wiki.
shapeBothBody: The map and the wiki side by side, with the wiki able to propose concepts to the map.
